_README: Shared fixtures for the server/client URL-decision differential test.
the "server" column against validateURLField) and web/src/util/safe-url.test.ts
(which asserts the "client" column against safeHref). Neither side can drift
without turning its own test red, and a case can only be silenced by editing
this file, which shows up in review.
This file exists because safe-url.ts used to claim the two guards agreed, so
that "a scheme the client allows and the server rejects is unreachable". The
SCHEME SETS agree. The DECISIONS do not: 9 of these 42 inputs are decided
differently. Every divergence is recorded below with a measured reason.
SECURITY READING: none of the 9 is a scheme escalation. In every case where
the client is the more permissive of the two, the input resolves to an http(s)
URL -- an attacker-chosen HOST, which is already reachable through a plainly
accepted https://evil.com/, and not an attacker-chosen SCHEME. They are
broken-link and inconsistency bugs, not XSS. Do not delete a case because it
looks harmless; the point is that the disagreement is pinned and bounded.
"accept" for the server means validateURLField returns nil. "accept" for the
client means safeHref returns the input unchanged.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Deliberate on both sides. The server treats "" as "unset" so callers can clear the field; the client renders no link for it. Same outcome, different vocabulary.

cases.name: backslash host confusion
cases.note: WHATWG reads the backslashes as slashes: new URL() yields host "evil.com" and the browser navigates there. net/url yields Host == "" and the server's host check rejects it. Client is MORE permissive.

cases.name: single slash host
cases.note: WHATWG normalises to http://example.com/ (host "example.com"); net/url treats it as an opaque/rootless path with Host == "".

cases.name: opaque no slash
cases.note: Same as above with no slash at all: WHATWG yields host "example.com", net/url yields Host == "".

cases.name: bare space in path
cases.note: Rejected by the server's control-character pre-check (space <= ' '). WHATWG percent-encodes it to /a%20b and accepts.

cases.name: trailing newline
cases.note: Rejected by the server's control-character pre-check. WHATWG strips ASCII newlines before parsing, so the client sees a clean URL.

cases.name: bad percent escape
cases.note: net/url errors on an invalid escape sequence; WHATWG leaves %zz alone and accepts.

cases.name: out of range port
cases.note: Server is MORE permissive here: net/url does not range-check the port at Parse time, while new URL() throws on a port above 65535.

cases.name: empty host with path
cases.note: WHATWG collapses the empty authority and promotes the first path segment to the host: new URL("https:///x").hostname === "x". net/url yields Host == "" and the server rejects.
